question: The word "speculative" in the phrase "speculative contexts" most nearly means ________.

options.text: imaginary or theoretical, not yet proven

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. imaginary or theoretical, not yet proven.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"speculative"** means:

 
 
• Involving consideration or conjecture based on incomplete or uncertain information; theoretical or hypothetical. (काल्पनिक या सैद्धांतिक, अभी साबित नहीं हुआ)
 
 
 
• The correct meaning of "speculative" in the given context is **"imaginary or theoretical, not yet proven."**
 
• **Example from the passage:** The scientific study explored speculative contexts regarding the future of human evolution.
 
 
• **Example:** The essay delved into speculative topics about future technological advancements and their impact on society.
 
 

Therefore, the word “speculative” most nearly means: **imaginary or theoretical, not yet proven.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Based on facts and reality** (तथ्यों और वास्तविकता पर आधारित): Grounded in actual events and verified information.

 
 
• **Example:** The news article was based on facts and reality, providing a detailed report of the incident.
 
 
 
• **Involving careful financial investments** (सावधानीपूर्वक वित्तीय निवेश शामिल करना): Making cautious decisions regarding monetary investments.
 
 
• **Example:** He spent months analyzing the market before making speculative financial investments.
 
 
 
• **Detailed and comprehensive research** (विस्तृत और समग्र अनुसंधान): Thorough and extensive study or investigation.
 
 
• **Example:** The project required detailed and comprehensive research to ensure accuracy.
 
 

1c9:T1394,
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.
